title: T2ICount: Enhancing Cross-modal Understanding for Zero-Shot Counting
property: object count (text-specified zero-shot counting on real images)
reads: Four U-Net decoder feature maps from one denoising step at t=1 plus class-name text features; cross-attention maps at 12x12, 24x24, 48x48 only build the training background mask
trained_on: FSC-147 training split (3,659 images, point labels turned into density maps); fine-tunes the SD1.5 U-Net at 1/10 learning rate and trains a correction module and counter for 400 epochs
gradient_enters: No gradient enters a generator; the model is an image counter trained with L = L_reg + gamma L_RRC
unseen: yes for the FSC-147 test split, whose classes do not overlap training (MAE 11.76 objects per image); the split behind the 196-image FSC-147-S is not stated, and the counter is never used for guidance
headline: FSC-147 test (held-out classes) MAE 11.76 objects per image against 13.30 for GeCo; on 196 less-frequent-class images MAE 4.69 against 31.30 for CounTX; SD1.5, lower is better
copy_or_avoid: Copy the category-disjoint split and the test on the less dominant class; do not cite it as proof that word attention alone can count, because attention only supplies a background mask and was weak on category at t=1 (inferred)
